purpose: 100 distinct contextual mnemonic illustrations for adult B1–B2 idiom learning
note: Images are mnemonic scenes, not claims about historical etymology. Each sheet was generated separately; row-major cells are extracted into individual WebP assets. Original large sheets remain in the local work folder.

sheets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Create one production sprite sheet for adult English idiom memory cards. EXACTLY 4 columns by 4 rows, 16 equally sized square cells, overall square 2048x2048 if possible. Each cell is a separate independent vignette centered inside its exact quarter-width and quarter-height cell, ample safe margin (keep all scene elements inside central 76% of each cell). NO gutters, NO borders, NO words, NO letters, NO numbers, NO typography anywhere. Consistent calm tasteful editorial gouache and softly sculpted clay textures, dark graphite backgrounds #171b22, warm cream characters, restrained copper orange and powder blue accents. Simple clear readable scenes, ordinary adult people, friendly cinematic lighting, concrete memorable objects. Every cell must be visually different; avoid repeated compositions. No frightening imagery. The scene order is absolutely important: row-major left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Do not draw labels or the idiom phrases; depict only scenes.

(14) A walker follows a clear safe trail leading toward a distant inviting goal, a subtle railway track motif alongside. (15) An astonished adult finds an unexpected lovely gift descending gently from a clear blue patch of sky.
